mcq.q: The mean deviation about the mean of 10, 10, 12, 29, 27, 14, 20, 10 is:
mcq.explain: The mean is 16.5. Absolute deviations: 6.5, 6.5, 4.5, 12.5, 10.5, 2.5, 3.5, 6.5; their sum is 53. Mean deviation = sum ÷ n = 53/8 = 6.62. Signs are ignored — with signs, deviations from the mean would add to zero.
mcq.topic: Mean deviation
mcq.fast: Find the centre, add the distances |x − centre|, divide by n.

mcq.q: The mean deviation about the median of 2, 29, 19, 27, 4, 24, 12 is:
mcq.explain: The median is 19. Absolute deviations: 17, 10, 0, 8, 15, 5, 7; their sum is 62. Mean deviation = sum ÷ n = 62/7 = 8.86. Signs are ignored — with signs, deviations from the mean would add to zero.
mcq.topic: Mean deviation
mcq.fast: Find the centre, add the distances |x − centre|, divide by n.

mcq.q: The mean deviation about the mean of 38, 31, 13, 16, 32 is:
mcq.explain: The mean is 26. Absolute deviations: 12, 5, 13, 10, 6; their sum is 46. Mean deviation = sum ÷ n = 46/5 = 9.2. Signs are ignored — with signs, deviations from the mean would add to zero.
mcq.topic: Mean deviation
mcq.fast: Find the centre, add the distances |x − centre|, divide by n.

mcq.q: The standard deviation of 24, 24, 17, 1 is about:
mcq.explain: Mean = 16.5. Squared deviations: 56.25, 56.25, 0.25, 240.25; sum = 353. Variance = sum/n = 88.25 and SD = √88.25 ≈ 9.39. Giving the variance as the SD (forgetting the root) is the trap.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance = mean of squares − (mean)²; then take the square root.

mcq.q: The standard deviation of 21, 28, 19, 22 is about:
mcq.explain: Mean = 22.5. Squared deviations: 2.25, 30.25, 12.25, 0.25; sum = 45. Variance = sum/n = 11.25 and SD = √11.25 ≈ 3.35. Giving the variance as the SD (forgetting the root) is the trap.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance = mean of squares − (mean)²; then take the square root.

mcq.q: The standard deviation of 14, 13, 26, 27, 12, 4 is about:
mcq.explain: Mean = 16. Squared deviations: 4, 9, 100, 121, 16, 144; sum = 394. Variance = sum/n = 65.67 and SD = √65.67 ≈ 8.1. Giving the variance as the SD (forgetting the root) is the trap.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance = mean of squares − (mean)²; then take the square root.

mcq.q: For 17 observations, Σx = 663 and Σx² = 27,234. The standard deviation is:
mcq.explain: Mean = Σx/n = 663/17 = 39. Variance = Σx²/n − (mean)² = 27,234/17 − 39² = 1602 − 1521 = 81. SD = √81 = 9. Forgetting to subtract the square of the mean, or forgetting the final square root, are the two common slips.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance = Σx²/n minus the square of Σx/n.

mcq.q: For 38 observations, Σx = 1,178 and Σx² = 37,468. The standard deviation is:
mcq.explain: Mean = Σx/n = 1,178/38 = 31. Variance = Σx²/n − (mean)² = 37,468/38 − 31² = 986 − 961 = 25. SD = √25 = 5. Forgetting to subtract the square of the mean, or forgetting the final square root, are the two common slips.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance = Σx²/n minus the square of Σx/n.

mcq.q: Series A: mean 31, SD 21. Series B: mean 48, SD 20. Which series is more consistent?
mcq.explain: Compare coefficients of variation, not SDs: CV(A) = 21/31 × 100 = 67.74%, CV(B) = 20/48 × 100 = 41.67%. The lower CV means less relative variation, so Series B is more consistent. Comparing the SDs directly would mislead because the means differ.
mcq.topic: Why dispersion? Absolute vs relative measures
mcq.fast: Lower SD/mean ratio = more consistent.

mcq.q: The coefficient of variation of a series is 15% and its mean is 195. Its variance is:
mcq.explain: CV = SD/mean × 100 ⇒ SD = CV × mean/100 = 15 × 195/100 = 29.25. Variance = SD² = 855.56. Stopping at the SD (29.25) answers a different question, so read whether the SD or the variance is asked.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: SD = CV% × mean; variance = SD squared.

mcq.q: A series has mean 164 and standard deviation 23. Its coefficient of variation is:
mcq.explain: CV = (SD ÷ mean) × 100 = 23/164 × 100 = 14.02%. It is a relative measure, free of units, so it compares the consistency of series with different means. A lower CV means a more consistent (less variable) series.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Coefficient of variation = SD ÷ mean × 100.

mcq.q: A series has mean 30 and standard deviation 29. Its coefficient of variation is:
mcq.explain: CV = (SD ÷ mean) × 100 = 29/30 × 100 = 96.67%. It is a relative measure, free of units, so it compares the consistency of series with different means. A lower CV means a more consistent (less variable) series.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Coefficient of variation = SD ÷ mean × 100.

mcq.q: If Q₁ = 21 and Q₃ = 51, the quartile deviation is:
mcq.explain: Quartile deviation (semi-interquartile range) = (Q₃ − Q₁)/2 = (51 − 21)/2 = 15. It ignores the top and bottom 25% of the data, so extreme values do not affect it. It is the preferred measure of spread for open-ended distributions.
mcq.topic: Quartile deviation and choosing a measure
mcq.fast: Half the gap between Q₃ and Q₁.

mcq.q: If Q₁ = 71 and Q₃ = 75, the quartile deviation is:
mcq.explain: Quartile deviation (semi-interquartile range) = (Q₃ − Q₁)/2 = (75 − 71)/2 = 2. It ignores the top and bottom 25% of the data, so extreme values do not affect it. It is the preferred measure of spread for open-ended distributions.
mcq.topic: Quartile deviation and choosing a measure
mcq.fast: Half the gap between Q₃ and Q₁.

mcq.q: If Q₁ = 64 and Q₃ = 118, the coefficient of quartile deviation is:
mcq.explain: Coefficient of QD = (Q₃ − Q₁)/(Q₃ + Q₁) = (118 − 64)/(118 + 64) = 54/182 = 0.2967. As a relative measure it has no units, so it can compare the spread of two series measured in different units.
mcq.topic: Quartile deviation and choosing a measure
mcq.fast: (Q₃ − Q₁) ÷ (Q₃ + Q₁).

mcq.q: The variance of the first 5 natural numbers is:
mcq.explain: For 1, 2, …, n the variance is (n² − 1)/12 = (25 − 1)/12 = 2. The mean is (n + 1)/2 = 3, which is a different measure. The SD would be √2.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance of 1…n = (n² − 1)/12.

mcq.q: The variance of the first 9 natural numbers is:
mcq.explain: For 1, 2, …, n the variance is (n² − 1)/12 = (81 − 1)/12 = 6.67. The mean is (n + 1)/2 = 5, which is a different measure. The SD would be √6.67.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Variance of 1…n = (n² − 1)/12.

mcq.q: The standard deviation of the two numbers 82 and 63 is:
mcq.explain: For two values the mean is (82 + 63)/2 and each value is |a − b|/2 = 9.5 away from it. So SD = √[(d² + d²)/2] = |a − b|/2 = 9.5. Range is 19, twice the SD here.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: SD of two numbers = half their difference.

mcq.q: If y = −4x + 29 and the range of x is 15, the range of y is:
mcq.explain: Adding a constant (29) shifts every value equally, so it does not change spread (change of origin). Multiplying by -4 scales spread by |-4| (change of scale); variance scales by -4² = 16. So the range of y = |-4| × 15 = 60. Measures of dispersion are never negative.
mcq.topic: Range and coefficient of range
mcq.fast: Ignore the added constant; multiply by |b| (or b² for variance).

mcq.q: If y = 3x − 11 and the variance of x is 14, the variance of y is:
mcq.explain: Adding a constant (-11) shifts every value equally, so it does not change spread (change of origin). Multiplying by 3 scales spread by |3| (change of scale); variance scales by 3² = 9. So the variance of y = 9 × 14 = 126. Measures of dispersion are never negative.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Ignore the added constant; multiply by |b| (or b² for variance).

mcq.q: If y = 2x − 3 and the range of x is 2, the range of y is:
mcq.explain: Adding a constant (-3) shifts every value equally, so it does not change spread (change of origin). Multiplying by 2 scales spread by |2| (change of scale); variance scales by 2² = 4. So the range of y = |2| × 2 = 4. Measures of dispersion are never negative.
mcq.topic: Range and coefficient of range
mcq.fast: Ignore the added constant; multiply by |b| (or b² for variance).

mcq.q: Group 1: n = 57, mean 41, SD 6. Group 2: n = 36, mean 42, SD 5. The combined standard deviation is about:
mcq.explain: Combined mean = 41.39. Combined variance = [n₁(σ₁² + d₁²) + n₂(σ₂² + d₂²)]/(n₁ + n₂), where d = group mean − combined mean: d₁ = -0.39, d₂ = 0.61. This gives 31.9792, so SD ≈ 5.66. Averaging the SDs ignores the gap between the group means.
mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Find the combined mean first; add each group's d² to its σ² before weighting.

mcq.topic: Standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation
mcq.fast: Find the combined mean first; add each group's d² to its σ² before weighting.
